subject: anatomy
title: Bilaminar and trilaminar disc, gastrulation and neurulation

steps.tx: The embryo starts as a **bilaminar disc** in the second week. It has two layers, the **epiblast** and the **hypoblast**. The epiblast is the source of all three germ layers. The hypoblast contributes mainly to extraembryonic tissue and the prochordal plate.
steps.say: The embryo starts as a bilaminar disc in the second week. It has two layers, the epiblast and the hypoblast. The epiblast is the source of all three germ layers. The hypoblast contributes mainly to extraembryonic tissue and the prochordal plate.

steps.tx: **Gastrulation** happens in the third week. It converts the bilaminar disc into a **trilaminar disc** with ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. It is the start of morphogenesis. The first visible sign is the **primitive streak**, a midline furrow on the dorsal epiblast at the caudal end. The streak lets us define the head, tail, and left and right sides.

vis.alt: Schematic cross-section of the third-week human trilaminar germ disc showing ectoderm, mesoderm with notochord and somites, and endoderm, with clinical derivatives of each layer.
vis.caption: Trilaminar embryonic disc: gastrulation produces ectoderm, mesoderm (notochord, paraxial somites), and endoderm.

steps.tx: Cells that move through the streak follow fixed paths. Cells through the node become **notochord**. Cells from the lateral streak edges form **paraxial mesoderm**, which becomes somites. Mid-streak cells form intermediate mesoderm. Caudal cells form lateral plate mesoderm. The most caudal cells form extraembryonic mesoderm. The notochord then signals the overlying ectoderm.

rows: Urinary and genital systems, adrenal cortex

steps.tx: **Neurulation** follows. The notochord induces the ectoderm to form the **neural plate**. The plate folds into a **neural tube**. The neural crest arises at the edges of the folds. Closure starts in the middle and spreads both ways. In the fourth week, the anterior neuropore closes by day 25 and the posterior neuropore by day 28. Failed anterior closure causes anencephaly, and failed posterior closure causes rachischisis.

steps.tx: The three panels trace **neurulation** from a flat **neural plate** with raised folds, through a deepening groove, to a closed round **neural tube** beneath the surface. The notochord sits below as the inducer while neural crest cells gather at the fold edges and then migrate away. The lesson times closure to the fourth week, with failed anterior closure causing anencephaly and failed posterior closure causing rachischisis.
steps.say: This diagram shows neurulation in three stages. First the neural plate dimples between raised folds above the notochord. Then the folds rise around a groove with neural crest cells at their tips. Finally the folds meet to form a closed neural tube covered by surface ectoderm while crest cells migrate outward. The lesson teaches that the notochord induces this folding and that closure spreads from the middle, with the anterior pore closing around day 25 and the posterior pore around day 28.

vis.alt: The three panel diagram shows the neural plate folding through a groove into a closed neural tube above the notochord.
vis.caption: Neural plate folding into a groove then a closed tube, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Neural crest** cells give rise to many structures. These include dorsal root and autonomic ganglia, the **adrenal medulla**, melanocytes, Schwann cells, odontoblasts, and parafollicular C cells. The adrenal cortex, enamel and the thoracic duct are not neural crest derived. Defective crest migration causes Hirschsprung disease, albinism and some neurocristopathies.
